courses.name: Statistics I
courses.description: Introduces statistical reasoning and inference using simulation and theoretical methods.

courses.name: R Lab
courses.description: Uses R for graphics, correlation, tests and regression.

courses.name: Foundations of Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Develops generative-AI projects while considering responsible design and human consequences.
courses.prerequisites: CS-170 or CS-173 or DATA-201, or instructor permission.

courses.name: Data Analytics
courses.description: Introduces SQL and R for extracting, manipulating, analyzing and visualizing data.
courses.prerequisites: Students who completed DATA-200 may not enroll.

courses.name: Technology and Ethics
courses.description: Examines ethical issues raised by data, surveillance, automated systems and digital technologies.

courses.name: Digital Image Making
courses.description: Develops vector and raster graphics through digital drawing, rendering and retouching.

courses.name: Introduction to Computer Science
courses.description: Introduces computational problem solving, algorithms and high-level programming.
courses.prerequisites: No prior computer programming experience is assumed.

courses.name: Digital Musical Audio Processing
courses.description: Uses computational techniques to synthesize, analyze, transform and retrieve musical audio, including Fourier methods and source separation.
courses.prerequisites: MATH-106 or 111 or higher and CS-174 (or CS-173 with permission of the instructor)

courses.name: Database Design
courses.description: Studies database models, design, queries and applications.

courses.name: Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Explores intelligent-system methods, knowledge representation, learning, search and responsible AI.
courses.prerequisites: Published wording: MATH-106 or MATH-111 or higher and CS-271 or 274.

courses.name: R for Data Science
courses.description: Uses R to collect, manipulate, analyze and visualize real-world data.
courses.prerequisites: STAT-142 and either CIE-100, CIE-150 or CIE-200, or instructor permission.

courses.name: Data Care and Cleaning
courses.description: Uses Python for data preprocessing, cleaning and visualization.
courses.prerequisites: CS-170 or another course in Python programming.

courses.name: Data-Driven Insights and Society
courses.description: Develops database-management skills and a substantial data project.

courses.name: Topics in Data Analytics
courses.description: Examines a selected special topic in data analytics.

courses.name: Introduction to Digital Studies
courses.description: Examines digital literacy, access, privacy, identity and ethical technology use through projects.

courses.name: Probability
courses.description: Introduces probability distributions and transformations of random variables.

courses.name: Philosophy of Mind
courses.description: Explores consciousness, minds and their relation to brains and bodies.

courses.name: Statistics II
courses.description: Extends statistical analysis to regression, nonparametric methods and statistical software.
courses.prerequisites: Published wording: STAT-142 and STAT-141Q or MATH-442.

courses.name: Biostatistics
courses.description: Applies inferential statistics to biological data with statistical reporting.

courses.name: Decision making under uncertainty
courses.description: Studies evidence, prior beliefs and methods for decisions under uncertainty.

courses.name: Applied Regression Models
courses.description: Develops regression models, diagnostics and responses to invalid assumptions.
courses.prerequisites: STAT-242W, STAT-243W or ECON-300Q, or instructor permission.

courses.name: Statistical Modeling
courses.description: Studies theoretical foundations of regression, ANOVA and statistical inference.
courses.prerequisites: MATH-235 and MATH-442, or instructor permission.

requirements.title: Minor total
requirements.summary: Complete 24 semester hours, including at least 17 in the five required courses and 7–8 in electives.

requirements.title: Required courses
requirements.summary: Complete all five required courses; the source states at least 17 credits.

requirements.title: Elective options
requirements.summary: Choose 7–8 elective credits to reach the 24-credit minor total. The listed courses and coordinator-approved options are eligible.

requirements.title: Coordinator-approved alternatives
requirements.summary: Another course may count with coordinator approval when it supports a substantial AI project. AI-focused honors, research or independent study may also count with approval, and requires a shareable presentation of rationale, approach and socio-ethical issues via CoSA, CS/MATH/STAT-350 or another approved venue.

requirements.title: Required-course enrollment restrictions
requirements.summary: CS-357 requires CS-170, CS-173, DATA-201 or instructor permission. DATA-201 bars students who have completed DATA-200; the AI requirement list does not explicitly permit substituting DATA-200. STAT-141Q cannot be taken for credit after or concurrently with another statistics course, including AP Statistics. The R Lab entry separately recommends concurrent enrollment with STAT-141Q for statistics majors/minors; that wording is preserved rather than expanded into an AI-specific co-requisite.

requirements.title: Statistics elective credit exclusion
requirements.summary: Credit cannot be received for both STAT-242W and STAT-243W.

requirements.title: Satisfactory/unsatisfactory grading approval
requirements.summary: An S/S-/U course counts toward a minor only with its director’s permission; the director may specify a minimum grade. The elective grading choice allows up to two courses of at most four credits each, declared during the first two weeks, and excludes CIE-100/150/200. S means C-minus or above; S-minus is a passing D-range grade. Repeat credit is earned only once.

requirements.title: Study elsewhere and transfer approval
requirements.summary: Obtain adviser and Registrar/Provost/Academic Standards approval before outside coursework. Transfer requires a C or better and an official transcript; credit, not grades, transfers. Current students have a 20-credit cap for online or other mediated courses. Nonpartner international coursework requires a course-by-course WES evaluation.

requirements.title: Minor completion verification
requirements.summary: The public verification form lists courses for the minor and requires adviser and minor department chair signatures. Its revision date is 2/11; it is currently linked by the Registrar.

requirements.title: Conditional honors route
requirements.summary: If using an honors project, the AI coordinator’s approval and AI presentation requirements still apply. College honors normally requires a 3.3 overall or major GPA (a research-adviser nomination and Academic Standards approval may allow an exception), faculty and departmental approval, a proposal and first-semester 491 report/presentation followed by approved 492 work, and the honors committee’s project review. This is conditional on choosing honors, not an added requirement for every AI minor.

requirements.title: Unresolved overlap policy
requirements.summary: The AI page and general Study in Depth section publish no specific AI overlap limit. Other catalog minors refer to normal major/minor overlap limitations without defining their applicability to AI. No limit from another program is imported; confirmation remains outstanding. General graduation residency applies explicitly to the degree and major, so no numeric minor-residency rule is inferred.

notes: The 2026–2027 catalog and live program requirements agree on all five required codes and 17 named elective choices, plus coordinator-approved alternatives. The institutional semester-hour basis and each resolved course amount were checked in the catalog; no quarter/semester conversion is applied.

Program-listed codes and stable IDs are retained. Catalog descriptions name STAT-141Q, STAT-242W and STAT-243W; DATA-150 is cross-listed DATA/STAT-150 and PHIL/CS-243 has the reverse CS/PHIL-243 entry. These aliases do not create extra courses.

All 22 course titles, descriptions and credit amounts are verified. The previously missed CS-372 appears as the cross-listed CS/MUS-372 in the department directory and current catalog; the program’s original code and stable ID are retained. A missing prerequisite remains unverified, not evidence of no prerequisite.
Overlap rules remain unresolved, so the curriculum is partial despite the expanded catalog and policy review. No AI minor GPA or residency amount is inferred from another minor or the host degree.
The catalog program introduction describes aims, not an explicit assessed learning-outcome list. Source statement type and inferred topic taxonomy remain separate. First-offered date unknown.

Follow-up review of the catalog Study in Depth/minor section, academic policies, registrar minor verification form and departmental overlap references still did not establish the general overlap limit applicable to AI. Two-course caps from business minors are not imported. Current CS/MUS-372 catalog inclusion resolves the missing-identity gap but does not promise a particular term offering.
